key_insight: Choosing the molecular enantiomer reverses polarization and persistent spin direction in two-dimensional chiral lead-halide perovskites.
engineering_relevance: These materials offer molecular control of nanoscale spin textures for potential spintronic devices, rather than a demonstrated solar-cell efficiency improvement.
method: Derived symmetry-allowed spin–orbit interactions for polar chiral perovskites.
Calculated first-principles spin textures for ten compounds, their mirror enantiomers and four halide-substituted analogues.
Ranked 34 two-band k·p models by spin-direction agreement rather than band-energy fits.
evidence_signal: For strongly polar compounds, the persistent-only conduction-band model achieved spin agreement ≥0.98 versus 0.20 for the best Rashba or Dresselhaus model, with coupling strengths of 1.09–1.98 eV Å and predicted spin-helix wavelengths of 3.4–8.2 nm.
watch_item: The abstract reports computational predictions, not experimental validation of persistent spin transport or photovoltaic performance.
paper_title: Polarization-locked chiral persistent spin textures in two-dimensional lead-halide perovskites
